the ship-conveying, dark-robed sacred vessel. Thus I corrected what is in M: τὰν ἄστονον μελάγκροκον | ναύστολον θεωρίδα [the ship-conveying, dark-robed sacred vessel]. ναύστολον [ship-conveying] is nowhere else read, except in the obscure gloss of Photius ναυστολοῦν : ναύστολον [conveying by ship: ship-conveying]. The scholiast explains: τὴν διάγουσαν τοὺς νεκρούς [the one conveying the dead]. And in another scholium ναύστολον θεωρίδα [ship-conveying sacred vessel]: he called the ship of Charon a sacred vessel. Properly, the one going to Delos belongs to Apollo. He says that she knows this as a sacred mission (thus I corrected what is in M: ταύτην ὁδὸν θεωρητικήν [this way as a sacred mission]), just as the groan knows the way to Acheron, the sunless one, which not even the sun sees, or the breath; for that one going to Delos is pure. θεωρίδα [sacred vessel] seemed to Hermann to be understood not of the ship but of the way, comparing the gloss of Hesychius θεωροί [sacred envoys]: they also call the road by which they go to the sacred rites θεωρίδα [sacred way], as θεωρικὴ ὁδός [sacred road] is noted by Pollux 2, 55, which does not suit the epithets ναύστολον μελάγκροκον [ship-conveying, dark-robed], fitting only the name of a ship.
